technology.summary: Today's technology news includes Microsoft's announcement of its third-generation Maia in-house AI chip, which will make the company less reliant on Nvidia's GPUs. The Fitbit Edge fitness tracker has also been officially launched, and a former Plaud exec has raised $26 million for an AI app that listens to users in the background. Amazon's use of over 1 million robot workers is also a topic of discussion, as is the upcoming Apple "Welcome Home" launch event, where smart home-related announcements are expected.

finance.summary:
The Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Reserve Bank of India have joined forces to make it easier for foreign portfolio investors to enter the market. This comes as Indian equity benchmarks experienced a decline over two sessions due to profit booking and rising oil prices, and as the Nifty 50 index closed down by 95.75 points, reaching 22,620.45.

Meanwhile, the Supreme Court of India has urged a probe into reports of patients being directed to specific pharmacies for their medications, following a landmark ruling highlighting troubling markups on cancer drugs enforced by hospitals.

In other news, a resurgent El Niño pattern risks deepening a selloff in Southeast Asian bonds, threatening to push yields higher just as rising US Treasury rates and oil prices squeeze regional debt.

citations.headline: Sebi, RBI join hands to make onboarding easier for FPIs
Stocks in news: Infosys, HDFC Bank, Jio Financial, IRFC, NCC and Blue Dart
Hospital stocks slip after SC query on steep cancer drug markups

politics.summary: Today's most important politics news includes the Delhi High Court's dismissal of pleas for an SIT probe into the 2020 riots and 2019 Jamia violence, as well as the Supreme Court's decision to list a plea to allow peaceful protests at Jantar Mantar. Congress has condemned the detention of tribal students headed for a protest in Mumbai, while Jairam Ramesh has criticised the CEC's ability to execute illegal orders. In other news, former US President Donald Trump has mistakenly cited an Indian election that didn't happen to call the US electoral process 'corrupt', and Bengali actor Koel Mallick has joined the BJP.
